newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore cuts economic growth outlook.
newsitem.headline: Singapore cuts economic growth outlook.

text.p: Singapore cut forecast 1996 and 1997 gross domestic product (GDP) growth on Tuesday, confirming analysts' expectations of a sharp slowdown in the economy.
Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong said in a speech that 1996 growth has been revised to about six percent from an earlier target of seven to eight percent.
He said said that growth in 1997 would be five to seven percent, slightly lower than the government's projected medium- term growth potential of six to eight percent.
A recent poll of economists by Reuters had put forecast 1996 GDP growth at 6.4 percent.
Lee also disclosed that 1996 third quarter GDP growth has slumped to 3.2 percent, down from the second quarter's 7.5 percent and 11.4 percent in the first quarter.
Singapore has been hit by a worldwide slowdown in the critical electronics sector, which accounts for 44 percent of the value added in Singapore manufacturing.
"A major reason for this downturn is the weak performance of manufacturing, particularly the electronics industry and related supporting industries," Lee said.
He said several other manufacturing industries are also weak, including ship-repair, printing, petrochemicals and pharmaceuticals.
Lee said the Ministry of Trade and Industry assessed the current slowdown as cyclical.
